oldPassage.sample: - **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the
oldPassage.text:
- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. An entry served by another pool is accepted and never run until the lease routes pools; a cell with no entry for the family's pool counts as a missing tier, which still falls back to the executor's own `model` or the CLI default. *(Superseded by RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool): every entry is a candidate of the walk, run when its pool can serve the invocation, and a family with no cell at the tier refuses `tier-cell-missing`; the `executor.model` and CLI-default fallthrough is deleted.)* The project config accepts every form. The global `~/.fgos/config.json` is read by every fgOS release on the machine, and an older release fails on a list and passes `model@pool` to the CLI as a model id, so a list or `@` cell there is dropped with a warning naming the cell (once per process), and doctor `global-model-policies-portable` fails on it. Each agent family (`providerModel`) is served by exactly one executor; its transports (headless cli, herdr pane, sandboxed or not) are invocations of that executor, and `bind()` picks the pane invocation inside herdr and a cli one outside, so a capability gets the same family and model in both places. Doctor `executor-family-unique` fails on a family with two agent executors. `runner.llmAccounts..` is the machine's account inventory, global-only: `credentialStore: { : }` (`~`, `${HOME}` and `$HOME` expand), plus optional `label` and `disabled`. A pool name is the family name for the family's own vendor and the provider's name otherwise (`openrouter`); it may not contain `@` nor be another spelling of a configured family (`codex`, `openai-codex`, `glm`, `agy`). `readLlmAccounts` reports problems instead of throwing; `compareWithLegacyInventory` sets it against `runner.providers..accounts` by the state key the lease uses (`openai` is `openai-codex` there). The lease, account pins and credential provisioning read a pool from `runner.llmAccounts` when it declares the pool, and from `runner.providers` for a pool it does not declare (the transition read, RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool)). Doctor: `llm-accounts-shape` fails on any reader problem, `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` warns on accounts or login directories that differ once `llmAccounts` is declared (the comparison stays needed while both inventories are read), `model-policy-pools` warns on a cell naming a pool `llmAccounts` does not declare (the walk skips such an entry), `tier-fallback` warns on a family `runner.tierFallback` lists that has no cell at that tier or no agent executor. `fgos dispatch explain --for [--rigor ]` binds the capability through `bind()` and reports the family and the `prefer` entry that chose it, the tier, its source (rigor, override) and its ceiling (RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling)), the candidates in walk order (each with the reason it is out: `tier-cell-missing`, `pool-unusable`), the walk a seat takes when each binding fails, the entries of the primary's cell (`used`, `fallback`, `unusable` with the reason), and the accounts of every pool on the walk in the order the lease takes them with whether the CLI can run on each. It leases, spawns and writes nothing. - **RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling, 2026-10-17).** `runner.maxTier`, when set, is the highest tier a seat runs at, whatever asked for the tier: the unit's rigor, the capability's rigor floor, or an override (`--override '{"tier":...}'`). A capability that declares its own `rigor` in `runner.capabilities` raises the ceiling for its own seats to `rigorToTier[rigor]` when that tier is higher. The ceiling of a seat is therefore the higher of `runner.maxTier` and the tier of its capability's declared rigor (`resolveTierCeiling` in `bind.mjs`); a unit's rigor and an override stay under it, so only the config decides which capabilities may run above the cap, and a frontier override on a capability declaring `high` stops at `flagship`. Without `runner.maxTier` there is no ceiling. A capability cannot be held below the global cap this way. The binding records the ceiling on `provenance.tier.ceiling` as `{ value, source }`, `source` being `global` or `capability-rigor(, )`; a clamped tier's source reads `clamped:maxTier(, )`. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the ceiling, and doctor `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted above `runner.maxTier` with the tier and model they run at; it never fails. The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose. - **RUL104 (`fgos run --resume` after a controller death takes the settled attempt through adopt and never runs the agent twice; Ctrl-C cancels; 2026-10-18; owner decision 2026-10-16).** A unit whose controller died never continues on its own: it reads `unitState: awaiting-resume` (last attempt `closed`, no `unit-summary.json`, no live controller; shown by `dispatch inspect`, `dispatch show-run` and `fgos run --json`) and only an explicit `--resume` goes on. Resume asks adopt about the last attempt of every seat and round before anything else: `closed` with a result is the attempt's result and the unit carries on from it (commit `writes`, reviewer, next attempt, `unit-summary.json`), so the agent runs once; a `cancelled`, `abandoned-not-started` or `abandoned-before-brief` receipt is superseded, a new attempt runs the unit again and names the old one in `supersedesRunId` (set only on a new launch; the old attempt reads `superseded`); a `gate-lost` receipt (binding present, gate dead, no `gate-exit`) is not relaunched, a named limit: adopt cannot prove the agent never ran, so it fails closed (r6 §9.7) rather than risk running it twice, and the person starts a new `fgos run`; `running` and `being-adopted` are refused `attempt-still-running` (resume does not wait); `legacy-run` is refused `attempt-legacy-run` (doctor `legacy-attempts-stuck` settles it as `abandoned-legacy`, which is closed for the unit); a second concurrent `--resume` of the unit finds the controller seat (`unit-control` ledger) held by a live controller and is refused `resume-in-progress`. Resume never starts a second supervisor for an attempt that already has a binding or a receipt. Ctrl-C or SIGTERM publishes `cancel-requested.json` for every attempt the controller handed over, waits for their receipts for at most `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` (default `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` + 5000, minimum 1000) and exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) after printing the resume command; a second signal exits at once. `fgos dispatch recover` over a supervised attempt recommends `adopt`; `outbox/result-N.json` is evidence for it, never a reason to park. Mechanism and tables: [run-supervisor spec, section 9.1](../platform/run-supervisor/spec.md#91-controller-death). - **RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads; the driver hands over exactly that store's files, 2026-10-19).** A confined `cli` invocation may declare `credentialStore: { use, homeEnv, files? }` in the config: `use` is the store key (`codex`, `pi`, `omp`, a lowercase key; it replaces the basename of `command` as the key into an account's `credentialSources`), `homeEnv` is the environment variable its CLI reads its login home from, and `files` (optional, non-empty, relative, no `..`, no repeats) lists what to hand over. The config door refuses a malformed store and a store on an invocation with no confinement backend (an unconfined invocation reads its store in place through `env`; that path is not redesigned). One function, `credentialStoreOf` (`provider-capacity.mjs`), reads it for every consumer; an invocation that declares none but binds `private-home` to an env variable (the machine-global config and other projects still carry that older form) gets `{ use: , homeEnv: }`, and that inference is the only remaining reader of `resourceBindings`; it goes when those configs have moved. The confinement request carries `invocation.credentialStore` in place of the generic `resourceBindings` (the contract keeps its name `confinement-request.v1`; nothing outside the repo reads the field). The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. Trust seeding, write-back and refresh-ahead keep reading the leased account's store, now chosen by the store key. `dispatch explain` names the store of the bound invocation and whether it is declared or inferred; `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` (same id) covers every confined invocation that reads a store, notes absent files and fails only when none is present. In this repo's committed config the invocations of one CLI under one executor collapse into one (`pi-cli-bwrap`; the account is leased at launch), invocation ids no longer carry an account name (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`), and the OpenRouter key variable left the pi `env` because pi reads the key from the store's `auth.json` (measured 2026-10-19: with the key variables unset and only the three store files, pi answered). Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active. - **RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order and its cell entries; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine are per pool; a missing cell refuses by name, 2026-10-20).** Owner decisions 2026-10-19 (plan `261019-2312-model-pool-b1-fallback-and-account-order`), the walk of RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)'s cells made real. **Candidates.** `bind()` expands each `prefer` executor into one candidate per entry of its family's cell at the seat's tier (RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)), in cell order: `{ executor, invocation, pool, model }`; an entry without `@` is the family-named pool. `provenance.model.source` reads `modelPolicies..[]` (it read `resolveTierModel(.)`). A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept (24 hours by default; until a person closes it when `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` is `null`) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control`, `terminal-config` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** - **`verify` stays on the Unit.** `validateUnit` keeps `verify` (a non-empty shell command) and `skills` (a non-empty list of skill names, trimmed, de-duplicated) through validation, the units-file loader, the workflow template and the round; a registered workflow template may set both too. - **Where the verify command comes from.** `verifyCommandOf` (`patterns/reviewed.mjs`) reads the Unit's own `verify`, else its capability's `verify`, and nothing else; the `code-change` preset pins none (it used to name `npm test`, which no runner ever executed, so a reviewed run recorded a verify pass that checked nothing), and `params.verify` no longer counts. A reviewed run with no verify command still passes on its checkers but its result carries `verify: { ran: false, reason }`; a solo or panel run, which has no verify step, says nothing. - **One bounded runner.** The verify step runs through `runCommand` (`src/runner/goal-check.mjs`, the same runner `return` and `approve` use) in the Unit's worktree, for at most `runner.timeoutMs` (the existing key and default; no new key, so nothing new for setup or doctor to register). A non-zero exit, a command that could not start and one that ran past the limit are each a failed verify that becomes findings naming the status (`exited N`, `timed out after Nms`, `could not run`) and the last twenty lines of output; none of them hangs the run. - **One-liner flags.** `fgos run "" --input , --verify ""` set the Unit's `inputs` and `verify`; both are refused beside `--unit` or `--resume`, and an empty value is refused before any unit run exists. - **Skills reach `bind()`.** `bind()` skips an executor whose `supports.skills` (new optional key in the executor's `supports` block, a non-empty array of names) does not list every skill the Unit names; none left refuses with reason `skills-unavailable` naming the missing skills, and the session lead never takes over such a Unit inline. Only roles that do the Unit's work are asked for skills: checker and panel roles (`reviewer`, `red-team`, `tester`, `panelist*`, `synthesizer`) are chosen on independence alone. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11).

currentPassage.text:
- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. The brief for an `ak:cook` worker is `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md`. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11). - **`debate`: two sides soft, the judge hard.** `runDebate` (`patterns/debate.mjs`) dispatches `thesis` and `antithesis` read-only with `preferIndependentOf` each other (a shared family is reported, not refused), optionally a second round where each side gets only the other's round-1 result in `inputs`, then `judge` with `independentOf: [thesis, antithesis]` and every result as `inputs`. The judge's family differing from both sides is the one hard independence rule of the pattern; an unseatable judge is bind()'s named `independence` refusal (`policy-refusal` outcome), never a same-family ruling. The three roles are listed once, in `CHECKER_ROLES` of `bind.mjs`, so they never run inline or in-process and are not asked for the Unit's skills. `fgos doctor`'s pool-independence check drives the same pattern code, so a pool with too few families fails it before a run. `unit-summary` gives the sides seat kind `producer` and the judge `judge`.
